significance: A timber-and-stone kath kuni temple on a ridge some seven kilometres from Shimla, built by the Sen rulers around 1766 and credited to King Bhupendra Sen. It is one of the best known Mahavidya shrines in the Himachal hills.
story: Bhupendra Sen is said to have been asked in a vision by the goddess Tara to enshrine her, and a later king, Balbir Sen, was told in a similar vision to place the temple on the Tarav hilltop where it stands.
